ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows two straight insulated wires crossing at right angles in the plane of the page. The vertical wire carries current I downward. The horizontal wire carries current I to the right. The labeled quadrants are: quadrant 1 in the upper right, quadrant 2 in the upper left, quadrant 3 in the lower left, and quadrant 4 in the lower right. Reasoning: Use the right-hand rule for each wire separately. For the horizontal wire with current to the right, the magnetic field is out of the page above the wire and into the page below the wire. For the vertical wire with current downward, the magnetic field is out of the page on the right side of the wire and into the page on the left side of the wire. Quadrant 1 is above the horizontal wire and to the right of the vertical wire, so both magnetic fields point out of the page; they add and cannot cancel. Quadrant 3 is below the horizontal wire and to the left of the vertical wire, so both magnetic fields point into the page; they add and cannot cancel. Quadrant 2 is above the horizontal wire and to the left of the vertical wire, so the horizontal-wire field is out of the page while the vertical-wire field is into the page; they are opposite and can cancel if their magnitudes are equal. Quadrant 4 is below the horizontal wire and to the right of the vertical wire, so the horizontal-wire field is into the page while the vertical-wire field is out of the page; they are also opposite and can cancel if their magnitudes are equal. Since the currents are equal and the field magnitude from a long straight wire is proportional to I/r, equal magnitudes occur where the perpendicular distances to the two wires are equal. Therefore zero magnetic induction is possible only in quadrants 2 and 4.

raw_record.question_text: In a plane, there are two perpendicular but insulated wires intersecting each other, with equal currents flowing through each wire in the directions shown in the image. In which quadrants might there be points where the magnetic induction is zero?

method.method_draft: First describe the image: identify the current directions and the four labeled quadrants. For each quadrant, use the right-hand rule separately for the horizontal wire and the vertical wire to decide whether each magnetic field points into or out of the page. In quadrant 1 the two fields have the same page-normal direction, and in quadrant 3 they also have the same direction, so they cannot cancel. In quadrant 2 the two fields are opposite, and in quadrant 4 the two fields are opposite. Because the currents are equal and field magnitude is proportional to I/r, points in those opposite-direction quadrants can have equal magnitudes when their perpendicular distances to the two wires are equal. Therefore possible zero-field points occur only in quadrants 2 and 4.

method.method_draft: First describe the image and define signed coordinates relative to the wire intersection. Let a candidate point be (x,y), excluding the wires. From the right-hand rule, the horizontal rightward current gives a signed page-normal field C/y, while the vertical downward current gives C/x, where C = μ0I/(2π) up to the same sign convention. The net field is therefore proportional to 1/x + 1/y. Setting this to zero gives 1/x + 1/y = 0, so x + y = 0, i.e. y = -x. This condition requires x and y to have opposite signs. Opposite signs place the point only in the upper-left and lower-right regions of the diagram, which are labeled quadrants 2 and 4.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中有两根互相垂直且相交的直导线，一根竖直、一根水平。竖直导线中的电流 I 方向向下；水平导线中的电流 I 方向向右。交点周围四个区域标为象限：右上为 1，左上为 2，左下为 3，右下为 4。

推理：以两导线交点为原点，水平向右为 x 正方向，竖直向上为 y 正方向。候选点为 (x,y)，且不在导线上，所以 x≠0、y≠0。两根导线电流大小相等，因此磁感应强度大小都与到导线的距离成反比。按右手定则并采用同一页法线正方向，水平向右电流在点 (x,y) 处产生的有符号磁场可写为 C/y；竖直向下电流在点 (x,y) 处产生的有符号磁场可写为 C/x，其中 C=μ0I/(2π)。因此总磁场正比于 1/x + 1/y。要使磁感应强度为零，需要 1/x + 1/y = 0，即 x + y = 0，也就是 y = -x。这要求 x 和 y 异号。x、y 异号对应左上象限和右下象限，即图中的第 2 象限和第 4 象限。
